A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MRGPRs are involved in the development of acute pain and, thus, might be a promising novel target to treat acute pain.
MRGPRX1, a neuropeptide receptor that induces acute pain, also promotes chronic pain via activation of SRF and NFAT signaling in DRG neurons.

the primate-specific MRGPR-X receptors are able to induce expression of chronic markers of pain, such as SRF and NFAT, and to promote the expression of the chemokines CCR2 and CCL2, which are both involved in pain chronification.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the primate-specific G protein-coupling receptor MRGPR-X, which is highly enriched in DRG neurons, is involved in the regulation of chemokine receptor expression and release of chemokines, and thus might contribute to the onset of chronic pain.

the neuropeptides MRGPR-X2 and MRGPR-X3, which are highly expressed by primate DRG neurons, are able to induce the expression of chemokine receptor CCR2, which in turn promotes the release of its endogen ligand CCL2 from human LAD-2 mast cells.
MRGPRX1 can activate two distinct pathways in DRG neurons: one that is mediated by SRF and ERKs and the second one that is mediated via NFAT.
